decisions.quote: In the absence of the beacon, participants in group Ambient tended to make path choices in the test that were adjacent to the location of the path that led away from the central chamber during the training phase. This pattern does not conform to that anticipated by Tolman et al., which assumes path choices in the test that were based on the shortest route to the goal location experienced during training. However, in group Light-Light, a close replication of the arrangement in the study of Tolman et al., path choices tended toward the paths leading to the goal/light.
decisions.reason: The close replication of Tolman et al.'s original arrangement with the goal-proximal light (group Light-Light) reproduced the original short-cutting choice pattern, whereas the conceptual replication removing the beacon confound (group Ambient) did not, which codes as mixed under the codebook rule for a close replication that works alongside a conceptual replication that does not.

parent_objection: The first review calls this mixed because the original light-present arrangement recovered goal-directed choices whereas the no-beacon condition failed. The paper frames the distinctive goal light as a potential confound and tests whether apparent shortcutting demonstrates an integrated cognitive map. Inspect abstract,results,and discussion to decide whether recovering the original effect while demonstrating invalid construct interpretation makes statistically successful but flawed the main-message verdict under the codebook, versus an authors overall failed or mixed verdict. A successful control does not automatically settle the whole replication. Use authors scope and comparisons,not the parent hypothesis.

shipped.title_o: Studies in spatial learning. I. Orientation and the short-cut.
shipped.outcome_quote: An experimental group, who followed the original procedure in the absence of any distinctive cues proximal to the goal, did not select the corridor which led most directly to the goal.

blind_target.title: Studies in spatial learning. I. Orientation and the short-cut.
blind_target.evidence_quote: This study replicated with human participants the essential features of the seminal short-cutting experiment by Tolman, Ritchie, and Kalish (1946) [14] with rats.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In the absence of the beacon, participants in group Ambient tended to make path choices in the test that were adjacent to the location of the path that led away from the central chamber during the training phase. This pattern does not conform to that anticipated by Tolman et al., which assumes path choices in the test that were based on the shortest route to the goal location experienced during training. However, in group Light-Light, a close replication of the arrangement in the study of Tolman et al., path choices tended toward the paths leading to the goal/light.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Close Light-Light replication agrees, Ambient conceptual replication does not. Explicit comparison across conditions settles mixed. Other cited short-cut studies supply context and are not independently re-tested.
